title: Kenyan Brownies
community: Urban Kenya — the café counter classic
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Brownies — rich, fudgy dark chocolate brownies made with Kenyan coffee for extra depth, with a crinkly top and gooey centre. The perfect café counter brownie — intense, slightly bittersweet, and impossible to eat just one of.
longDesc: The perfect brownie has been perfected at Nairobi's best cafés — fudgy rather than cakey, with that characteristic crinkly sugary top. The addition of Kenyan espresso amplifies the chocolate flavour without tasting of coffee.
steps: Preheat oven to 170°C. Grease and line tin.
Melt chocolate and butter together. Cool slightly.
Add eggs one at a time — whisk vigorously after each.
Fold in flour, cocoa, and salt. Do not over-mix.
The top should be set and crinkly; a skewer should come out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely before cutting — the fudgy centre sets as it cools.
chefTips: Under-bake slightly — fudgy brownies are the goal, not cakey.
Cool completely before cutting — cutting warm brownies produces crumbles.
The crinkly top comes from the vigorous whisking of eggs and sugar.
cookingScience: The crinkly top forms when sugar and egg foam rises to the surface during baking and sets as a meringue-like crust. The fudgy interior is achieved by a higher ratio of fat (chocolate and butter) to flour — the fat prevents the starch and protein networks from setting fully, keeping the centre soft.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan espresso in the brownies — supporting local coffee farmers.
culturalNote: Nairobi's café brownie culture has reached international standards — the best brownies in the city rival any served in London or New York, partly because of the extraordinary Kenyan coffee used in the batter.
